analysis: Examined base text of ClusterOnboardingLive.swift lines 1-893 plus the partial head patch. Changes: executeForwarded now passes request.scope to localPlanModels (head 272) and localAdopt (head 276); planModels sends context.settings.servingScope in the forwarded ClusterControlRequest (head 600-601); a new planningScope(named) resolves the scope from the forwarded request, then the local run setting, then the saved leadership.scope, defaulting to .publicServing (head ~606-612). Further changes at head 614-616, 633 and 1048-1084 are not visible in these units. Security relevance: the forwarded scope comes from the paired peer, which is authenticated by the link pairing (Secure Enclave pin) and the setup exchange. It influences planning mode and possibly adoption. The existing .scope op already accepts a peer-supplied scope (base 284-286), so a peer naming the scope is not new trust. The existing privateImageQualification refusal to forward is preserved (base 214-216). Defaulting to .publicServing selects the coordinator-oriented plan. That is not evidently a widening, but integration should confirm it. Integration questions: (1) Does localAdopt(scope:) persist the forwarded scope into the leader's record without the validation that localSetScope applies? The base .scope path rejects a nil or invalid address at 285. Does adopt validate an address-bearing scope the same way? (2) Do publicTraffic and qualification messaging (base 663-664) still apply under the new scope paths? (3) What changed at head 1048-1084? No regression is established from the visible evidence. These flows touch TB-011/T-052 only indirectly, through serving-scope labeling; no provider wire, attestation or cache (T-041) path changed here.
